about: Energy, range and speed (spec: Power and efficiency analysis, 'Range, endurance and speed'; analyzers/energy.py). Uncalibrated against real aircraft: checked on synthetic flights and in ArduPilot's simulator.

phases.about: Each steady tile's flight phase (analyzers/steady.py), from the primary estimator core's ground velocity in tile_s tiles of at least min_samples rows (the same tiles the wind analyzer and the sweep read): low when under min_height_m above take-off, whatever it does; a climb or descent at climb_ms or more up or down; else a hover under hover_speed_ms of ground speed; else level at level_speed_ms or more while it climbs or descends under level_climb_ms, accelerates under max_accel m/s/s and turns its track under max_turn_deg_s; anything else a manoeuvre. The power model's points and the energy breakdown are read by phase.

fast.about: The fast segment (analyzers/fast.py): the flight's level steady tiles (phases above) at share or more of its fastest, through the air (each tile's ground velocity less the flight's wind from the drag it measures itself, wind.json; else by ground speed), once the fastest reaches min_top_ms and the segment holds min_seconds. Vibration is the vibe_percentile percentile of the worst axis of any IMU; the motors' highest output the output_percentile percentile of the highest motor; the lean the lean_percentile percentile of the tilt.

flight.about: A flight's energy (analyzers/energy.py): the packs' power (rules/batteries.json, every monitor that measures its own pack) and the primary estimator core's horizontal ground speed, each integrated from arming to disarming by the trapezoid rule over every row; the energy split by each steady tile's phase. Energy per km is given once the flight covered at least min_distance_m over the ground, and at cruise once its level tiles did.

sweep.about: The speed sweep (procedure followup.speed_sweep): straight legs held at steady speeds, each flown both ways. The flight is cut into tile_s tiles of the primary estimator core (XKF1); a tile is level and steady when it holds at least min_samples rows, flies at least min_height_m above take-off, at a ground speed of at least min_speed_ms, accelerating under max_accel m/s/s, climbing or descending under max_climb m/s, and turning its track under max_turn_deg_s. Back-to-back steady tiles whose ground speed stays within leg_speed_ms of the leg's mean and whose track stays within leg_track_deg of its first tile make a leg; legs of at least min_leg_s count. A leg and the next one make a pair, flown both ways, when the next starts within pair_gap_s, heads within reciprocal_deg of the opposite way, and differs in ground speed by at most pair_speed_ms (twice the strongest wind the card allows, for a pilot holding the airspeed; ArduPilot holding WP_SPD keeps the two alike). A pair's speed is the mean of its two, which cancels the wind along the legs. Pairs sorted by speed split into levels where the next is more than level_gap_ms faster. The sweep is measured once min_levels levels are flown; the follow-up offers the card until a flight of the airframe in the same payload group has.
sources: Power against airspeed comes from level segments flown at steady speed: the minimum is the best-endurance speed and the tangent from the origin the best-range speed (Leishman, Principles of Helicopter Aerodynamics, 2nd ed., 2006, ch. 5, 'Performance'). On multirotors the curve's shape depends on payload and speed and is measured, not assumed (Rodrigues et al., In-flight positional and energy use data set of a DJI Matrice 100 quadcopter for small package delivery, Scientific Data 8, 2021, doi:10.1038/s41597-021-00930-x: legs at several speeds and three payloads).

Reciprocal legs: flying a leg both ways at one setpoint and averaging cancels the wind along it, the standard way to measure airspeed performance without an air-data sensor (FAA Advisory Circular 23-8C, Flight Test Guide, 2011, 'Airspeed calibration' ground-course method).

ArduPilot's simulator draws power in proportion to thrust (libraries/SITL/SIM_Motor.cpp at Copter-4.7.0: current = power_factor * |thrust| / voltage), so it shows no drop in power at moderate forward speed: the sweep has to be flown on the aircraft.

view.about: The Energy section of a flight's Propulsion view (energy_view.py), drawn on the laptop only. The breakdown splits the packs' energy into the ESCs' input by flight phase, the harness (the pack's voltage less the ESCs' median voltage, times the pack's current) and the avionics (what is left), only when every motor's ESC reports its voltage and current over the whole armed flight, never on the simulator (whose ESC current and voltage are placeholders), and only when the ESCs report no more than the packs give, within max_esc_excess of the energy used. Battery heat is each counted pack's current squared times its logged resistance. Climb energy per metre needs min_climb_m climbed in climb tiles. The airframe's curve is drawn at the flight's weight and mean air from 0 to the larger of curve_top_ms and its fastest point plus curve_margin_ms, every curve_step_ms, with the 95% band of the bootstrap's models once there are at least min_replicates; the flight's excess over the model fitted without it gets a 95% interval from interval_draws resamples of its points, seeded.
